newsitem.title: USA: Dow poised for run at 6000, profit-taking looms.
newsitem.headline: Dow poised for run at 6000, profit-taking looms.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to face early profit-taking following their rally Friday but despite the prospect of mild selling, analysts said the Dow industrials should manage a challenge of the 6000 level.
"We'll probably see some early profit-taking," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "But later in the session the market will make a stab at 6000."
Oil stocks are likely to lend early strength to the Dow industrials after a report that several industry giants are discussing a merger of their U.S. downstream operations.

The Wall Street Journal report was cited as pushing oil shares higher in Europe and said that Texaco Inc, Shell Oil Co and Saudi Aramco are discussing merging their U.S. refining and marketing businesses.
Whether or not the Dow's first run at 6000 occurs Monday, analysts said the average, if it holds to form, would need several sessions before successfully closing above the milestone.
"We'll probably cross and re-cross a number of times," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "Once we pass through, we'll probably get knocked down again."
Monday will offer markets little in the way of economic data. August consumer credit figures are due today, but not until 1500 EDT/1900 GMT, late in the day's trading session.
While the number serves as a barometer for consumer spending, this week's release by U.S. retailers of September sales figures will offer fresher information.
In Tokyo, stocks were little changed as markets await the outcome of Japan's general elections later this month. The Nikkei 225 rose 13 points to 21,161.
U.S. stocks were firmer in London, led by shares in oil companies. The FTSE 100 rose 10 points to 4034.
The dollar was steady in Tokyo and in Europe, holding near 111.5 yen and 1.53 marks.
Bonds were slightly softer. The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury fell 6/32 to yield 6.77 percent.
December S&P 500 index futures rose 0.2 to 707.35.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column examines AMR Corp's initial public offering of its SABRE computer reservation unit. According to the column, some analysts are questioning SABRE's long-term outlook, including what form the company's relationship with American Airlines will take.
